cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Bring Back Everything
cards.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I took away a chair like the caterer did. The cake can sit on the piano stool, and your uncle can have the window seat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She took away a broken chair. You've removed the only spare seat for the pianist.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, making a little room. The pianist can sit at the window until we're ready for music.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Uncle's there. And the cake's icing is melting; that window has to open, but the seat blocks it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then bring my chair back for Uncle, put the cake at the open window, and give the stool to the pianist. Every place I made comes back to that chair.

reason: Make the misunderstood copied act determine the same-holder Drive pursuit, preserve the useful original situation where possible, and give B4 specific causal material for A5.
